archetype.name: representative vegetative Escherichia coli cell
archetype.scopeNote: A generalized, non-dividing rod-shaped E. coli cell used to teach the stable Gram-negative envelope and core cytoplasmic organization. It is not a reconstruction of a named strain, growth condition, or cell-cycle stage.

representativeDimensions.interpretation: Representative teaching proportions only. E. coli size and aspect ratio vary with strain, medium, growth rate, cell-cycle stage, and perturbation.

archetype.requiredInterpretation: The model must read as a closed three-dimensional rod with rounded poles and nested envelope layers, not as a flat diagram. Molecular and ultrastructural details may be enlarged only when declared as didactic scale exaggerations.

globalConstraints.requirement: Preserve the outside-to-inside envelope order: outer membrane with LPS in its outer leaflet, periplasm containing a thin peptidoglycan sacculus, inner membrane, then cytoplasm.
The peptidoglycan must be much thinner than a Gram-positive wall and must lie within the periplasm, not outside the outer membrane.

Chromosomal DNA must occupy a non-membrane-bounded nucleoid in direct continuity with cytoplasm. Do not model a nucleus, nuclear envelope, nucleolus, mitochondria, Golgi apparatus, endoplasmic reticulum, chloroplasts, lysosomes, or other eukaryotic membrane-bound organelles.

Plasmids, flagella, fimbriae, conjugative pili, capsules, and extracellular polymers are optional strain- and condition-dependent features. If shown, they must be labeled optional rather than defining every E. coli cell.
Cut surfaces must reveal true shell thickness and internal depth; uncut rear, side, top, and bottom surfaces must remain closed and inspectable through a full orbit.
Generated turnaround or unseen-side views are synthetic hypotheses for composition and geometry only. They cannot establish anatomy, abundance, topology, scale, or scientific acceptance.

structures.label: Rod-shaped cell body
structures.geometry: A straight to gently irregular spherocylinder: a cylindrical sidewall with rounded poles and real volume. Use representative proportions near 2.5 micrometres long by 0.8-1.0 micrometres wide, while declaring the dimensions variable.
relationships: Envelope layers follow the same rod-and-rounded-pole topology
Cutaway does not collapse the rear or underside
avoid: A dividing septum unless the asset is explicitly changed to a division-stage variant

structures.label: Outer membrane and lipopolysaccharide (LPS)
structures.geometry: Continuous outer bilayer shell. Represent LPS as a molecularly simplified surface treatment of the outer leaflet, not as a separate membrane or thick capsule. Lipid A/core/O-antigen detail, if visible, is didactically enlarged and chemically generalized.
relationships: LPS is in the outer leaflet
avoid: Claiming a particular O-antigen or smooth-LPS chain length without a named strain/serotype

structures.label: Periplasm
structures.geometry: A continuous, narrow three-dimensional compartment between outer and inner membranes. Its width may be enlarged for legibility, but the legend must state that this is not literal scale.
avoid: Treating it as empty extracellular space
Placing ribosomes or chromosomal DNA in it

structures.label: Thin peptidoglycan sacculus
structures.geometry: A continuous, stress-bearing mesh-like shell inside the periplasm. It must be visibly thinner than the membrane-to-membrane periplasmic gap; any mesh spacing and strand thickness are enlarged teaching abstractions. Cryo-electron tomography places Gram-negative peptidoglycan at no more than about 4 nm in the examined sacculi.
avoid: Open discontinuous belt presented as the whole sacculus

structures.label: Inner membrane
structures.geometry: A continuous phospholipid bilayer shell immediately inside the periplasm, enclosing the cytoplasm. Bilayer thickness and embedded proteins may be enlarged for visibility.

structures.label: Cytoplasm
structures.geometry: A connected interior volume enclosed by the inner membrane, containing the nucleoid region, ribosomes, and soluble cellular material. It is crowded and organized, but should not be rendered as membrane-bounded subcompartments.

structures.label: Nucleoid (chromosomal DNA)
structures.geometry: A diffuse, irregular or lobed central DNA-rich region represented by a folded/supercoiled chromosomal-DNA network with associated proteins. It has no enclosing membrane. Avoid a single tidy ball or exact fixed loop pattern; organization changes with growth and replication.
relationships: May exclude many translating ribosomes from its densest regions
Represents the main bacterial chromosome rather than a eukaryotic nucleus
avoid: Chromosomes drawn as eukaryotic X shapes
Claiming one visible DNA loop equals the literal chromosome conformation

structures.label: 70S ribosomes
structures.geometry: Numerous small particles in the cytoplasm, with particle size and count reduced or enlarged for mobile legibility. A mildly ribosome-rich region outside dense nucleoid lobes is defensible, but no exact stationary pattern should be implied.
relationships: Not attached to rough ER because E. coli has no ER
Distribution relative to the nucleoid is dynamic and growth-condition dependent
avoid: A sparse handful presented as literal abundance

structures.label: Plasmid DNA
structures.geometry: Zero or a small number of compact, circular DNA loops in cytoplasm, spatially distinct enough for labeling. Visible diameter and separation are teaching exaggerations.
relationships: Separate from the main chromosome/nucleoid representation
avoid: Presenting plasmids as universal or essential
Claiming an exact copy number or gene cargo without a named plasmid and strain
structures.condition: Include only with an explicit 'optional; strain-dependent' qualifier. A plasmid-free representative state is scientifically acceptable.

structures.label: Flagellum
structures.geometry: If a motile flagellated state is selected, use one or more long helical filaments connected through hook/basal regions to the envelope. A peritrichous distribution over the cell surface is characteristic of flagellated E. coli, but filament number varies.
relationships: Much longer than fimbriae when drawn at comparable scale
avoid: Claiming every strain or cell is motile/flagellated
structures.condition: Optional and dependent on strain, genotype, expression state, and growth conditions.

structures.label: Fimbriae (adhesive pili)
structures.geometry: If selected, show many short, fine surface fibers that are clearly shorter than flagella. Their density is illustrative rather than a literal fixed count.
relationships: Terminology overlaps with 'pili' in the literature
avoid: Calling every short fiber a conjugative pilus
Floating or penetrating into cytoplasm without an envelope attachment
structures.condition: Optional; fimbrial gene content and expression are strain- and condition-dependent, and type 1 fimbriae can be phase-variable.

structures.label: Conjugative pilus
structures.geometry: At most a few longer surface filaments, clearly distinguishable from a dense fimbrial coat and connected to an envelope-spanning assembly platform when magnified.
relationships: Requires relevant conjugative genetic machinery, commonly plasmid encoded
Distinct educational role from adhesive fimbriae
avoid: Showing F-pilus machinery in a cell explicitly labeled plasmid-free
structures.condition: Include only in a specifically labeled conjugative/plasmid-bearing variant.

labelingRules: Use 'outer membrane' and 'inner membrane' as separate labels; 'cell membrane' alone is ambiguous in a Gram-negative bacterium.
Label LPS as part of the outer leaflet of the outer membrane, not as a standalone wall.
Label the compartment between the two membranes 'periplasm' and the thin mesh within it 'peptidoglycan sacculus'.
Use '70S ribosomes' without implying that visible particle size or count is literal.
Label plasmid DNA, flagella, fimbriae, conjugative pili, and any capsule as optional and strain/condition dependent.
If both fimbriae and a conjugative pilus are shown, distinguish their forms and functions in the legend while acknowledging overlapping terminology.
Any enlarged membrane, LPS molecule, peptidoglycan mesh, ribosome, DNA filament, or appendage diameter must be described as didactic scale exaggeration.
prohibitedMisconceptions: E. coli has a nucleus, nuclear membrane, nucleolus, mitochondria, Golgi apparatus, endoplasmic reticulum, chloroplasts, lysosomes, or other eukaryotic membrane-bound organelles.
The nucleoid is a membrane-bounded organelle.
Gram-negative E. coli has one membrane or a thick Gram-positive peptidoglycan wall.
LPS is located on the inner membrane or forms a separate third membrane.
The periplasm is the same compartment as cytoplasm.
Every E. coli cell carries plasmids, flagella, fimbriae, conjugative pili, or a capsule.
A representative cell has a fixed size, chromosome conformation, ribosome distribution, or appendage count.
acceptanceChecks: A 360-degree orbit confirms a volumetric rod with rounded poles and closed rear, side, top, and bottom geometry.
The cutaway preserves the outside-to-inside order: outer membrane/LPS, periplasm with thin peptidoglycan, inner membrane, cytoplasm.
Peptidoglycan is a thin sacculus within the periplasm rather than a thick external wall.
The nucleoid is visibly non-membrane-bounded and contains a plausible folded DNA network without eukaryotic chromosome forms.
Ribosomes occupy cytoplasm and do not occur in periplasm or on rough ER.
No nucleus, mitochondria, Golgi, ER, chloroplast, lysosome, or other eukaryotic membrane-bound organelle is present.
Every optional plasmid or appendage is disclosed as strain/condition dependent, and every filament has a continuous envelope attachment.
If flagella are included, their helical filaments are distinguishable from short fimbriae; if a conjugative pilus is included, it is distinguished from adhesive fimbriae.
A legend separates cell-scale proportions from enlarged molecular and ultrastructural details.
No generated or synthetic view is cited as scientific proof.

evidencePolicy.imageGenerationReferences: Synthetic or generated views are hypotheses for composition, occlusion, and unseen geometry only; they are never evidence for biological anatomy, abundance, topology, scale, or acceptance.
evidencePolicy.strainPolicy: Unnamed representative imagery cannot justify strain-specific O-antigen, capsule, plasmid, appendage, virulence, or motility claims.
evidencePolicy.conflictRule: When an image or generated view conflicts with this contract or the cited scientific literature, the contract and literature prevail.
